# Radoslav Radev Recommends The Planche Lean Hold To Learn Right Muscle Engagement And Technique For The Full Planche

Radoslav Radev recommends the planche lean hold as the progression to learn the right technique, muscle engagement, and understanding of how the planche works before starting the full planche. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 01:56]

## Details

- He says the second advice is to have the understanding of how the planche works, the biomechanics, and the right muscles to squeeze to learn the right technique. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 01:56]
- The planche lean hold gives you the opportunity to understand the logic, to push in the right direction, to squeeze the right muscles, and to breathe properly. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 02:12]
- You apply these things until the end of your planche career, even when you go from planche to maltese and other harder progressions. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 02:26]
- If you learn the right muscle engagement from the beginning, your whole planche journey will be much easier and you will not struggle because of wrong muscle engagement. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 02:38]
- He says he knows a lot of people who have a perfect program and train a lot but make mistakes in their technique that are really important not to make, and that is why they are stuck. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 02:48]
- Some mistakes in the planche can be carried into later progressions, and if you do not fix them you can end up with bad form that looks good for the planche hold but causes struggle on planche push-ups and planche presses. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 03:09]
- Wrong hips activation on the straddle planche sometimes looks good, but when you go from straddle to full planche the full planche is really formed. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 03:28]
- When you understand all these things from planche lean hold, tuck planche, and all the other progressions, you progress much faster and you will listen to your body much better about when to go to the next progressions. [src: vid-aXwZ_WI1vSw @ 03:48]
